== Biography ==
'''Mary Jane Glasgow''' was born about 1839 or 1840 in County Antrim, Ireland. An 1847 Ballymena Workhouse return records a nine-year-old Mary Jane Glasgow of Glenleslie in a family group with Mary, Boyd, William James and Margaret Glasgow.<ref name="Workhouse1847">[https://www.billmacafee.com/otherrecords/ballymenaworkhouse.pdf William Macafee, "Admissions to Ballymena Workhouse: 13th May to 8th July 1847"], registrations 4406–4410 (accessed 13 August 2026).</ref>

The surviving 1851 Ballycregagh census directly calls an eleven-year-old Mary Jain Glasgow a daughter of [[Glasgow-2981|James Glasgow]]. She was a weaver of yarn.<ref name="Census1851">1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy parish, Ballycraigargh, household 29, James Glasgow household: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22 living household, image 251] and [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-Y621 continuation and mortality return, image 252].</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-2981]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The held 1851 return explicitly names Mary Jain, eleven, as James’s daughter and yarn weaver. The workhouse transcription’s earlier same-name death is a conflict to resolve in that linkage, while it does not negate the 1851 daughter statement for this census-defined girl.

Held 1851 census relationship quotation/summary and existing source citations establish the census-defined child’s father; no fresh image inspection or adult identity extension.

Next useful test: Inspect the original 1847 death/discharge row against the 1851 daughter.

Source basis already held: [https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22 1851 Census of Ireland, County Antrim, Dunaghy parish, Ballycraigargh, household 29, James Glasgow household: living household, image 251 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G94X-YD22) and continuation and mortality return, image 252 (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L94X-Y621).]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



[[Hamilton-25516|Peggy Hamilton]] married James in 1848, years after Mary Jane's birth, and cannot be her mother. [[Unknown-764460|Mary]] in the 1847 workhouse group is the probable mother.

The workhouse transcription records its Mary Jane as dying on 27 November 1847, but the 1851 return records a same-named daughter alive at approximately the same age. This may be a transcription or return error; death remains unknown until the original records resolve it.

The [https://nationalarchives.ie/collections/search-the-census/search-results/#census_year=1851&surname__icontains=Glasgow&county=Antrim&parish__icontains=Dunaghy&townland__icontains=Ballycre&house_number=29&limit=30 National Archives of Ireland household link] cited on the profile is preserved.
